subject: Renewal: Exhibit E (usage tiers) + order form capacity increase
messages:
From: Samira Khan <contracts@pivotalhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Zhou <alice.zhou@pivotalhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal kick-off + Exhibit E clarification

Hi Neha,

We’re kicking off Pivotal’s renewal discussion for the Jan 2029 term and are planning a capacity uplift across several environments (prod burst, staging baseline). Legal is asking us to confirm Exhibit E usage tiers and whether the order form can include a short-term burst allowance for Q3.

Can you confirm Redwood’s position on: 
- short-term burst (30% above base) for 90 days
- how burst usage is metered/rounded on invoices
- whether Exhibit E can be amended without re-signing the MSA (we prefer minimal friction)

Attaching the draft order form we received from our procurement (order form v3). Alice is on copy for technical questions.

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Procurement | Pivotal Health
contracts@pivotalhealth.com

Attachments: Pivotal_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <contracts@pivotalhealth.com>
Cc: Alice Zhou <alice.zhou@pivotalhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal kick-off + Exhibit E clarification

Hi Samira — thanks for the note and the draft. Short answers up front: we can support a 90-day burst window, and we meter burst at per-token equivalent (rounded to nearest whole unit on invoice). Changes to Exhibit E that are purely schedule (usage tiers/pricing) can typically be handled as an order form amendment rather than an MSA re-sign, provided no material SLA or data handling changes are introduced.

I want to loop in our contracts and renewals folks to confirm the exact language and any limits. On our side I’ve attached a proposed Exhibit E table (ExhibitE_usage_tiers_proposal.xlsx) with how we would structure tiers + burst addendum.

I’ll follow up internally and share redlines to the order form and MSA if needed.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments: ExhibitE_usage_tiers_proposal.xlsx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 10:47:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal kick-off + Exhibit E clarification — need contract review and order form redlines

Folks — forwarding Pivotal’s draft and my proposal. Key asks: 90-day burst window (30% over base), language to allow Exhibit E schedule changes via order form amendment, and clarifying metering/rounding on invoices.

Can Legal/Offers confirm whether the following clause is acceptable?

Proposed burst addendum snippet:
"Customer may exceed baseline committed capacity by up to 30% for a contiguous period not to exceed 90 days ("Burst Window"). Such Burst usage will be billed at the Customer’s contracted per-unit rate and rounded to the nearest whole unit on the invoice. Temporary increases within the Burst Window shall not constitute a permanent amendment to Exhibit E."

If acceptable, please redline the attached MSA_redline_v2.docx and the order form. Also advise if Finance requires a minimum commit floor to enable burst.

Thanks — Neha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal kick-off + Exhibit E clarification — redlines attached

Neha — thanks. Drafted redlines attached. High-level notes: 
- Legal is comfortable with an Exhibit E schedule amendment via order form provided changes are limited to tiers/pricing and do not alter data handling obligations or core SLA definitions.
- Recommend limiting burst to 3 contiguous months per 12-month period to avoid perpetual elevated load.
- Finance flagged that burst billing should be prepaid or reconciled monthly depending on customer preference; recommended default is monthly reconciliation to avoid cash flow friction.

Attaching MSA_redline_v2.docx and a tracked-orderform PDF for clarity (Pivotal_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf).

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: MSA_redline_v2.docx; Pivotal_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf

From: Samira Khan <contracts@pivotalhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Zhou <alice.zhou@pivotalhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Apr 2028 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal kick-off + Exhibit E clarification — redlines attached

Neha/Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side after internal review: 
- Pivotal is okay with the 90-day burst but asks for a clear definition of "contiguous" and a cap on total burst-days per year (we proposed 120 days cumulative).
- For billing, Procurement prefers monthly reconciliation (good). Finance wants an option to prepay for a burst bucket; can Redwood offer a prepay credit mechanism?
- We also requested a small change in the order form: include an operational contact for emergency capacity increases (Alice listed but we need Redwood ops contact).

Attached are our in-document comments on the PDF. If we can get to agreement on these items, we can route the final order form for signature.

Best,
Samira

Attachments: Pivotal_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (comments)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Apr 2028 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal coordination — ops contact + prepay option proposal

Looping in our infra/ops POV: we can assign a dedicated operational contact (onsite rotation) for Pivotal and support emergency capacity increases with a 2-hour SLA for escalation routing during business hours. On prepay: Finance prefers a simple prepay credit account tied to the order form (prepaid credits consumed against burst usage, reconciled monthly). Suggested language for order form: 

"Customer may purchase prepaid Burst Credits that Redwood will apply against Burst usage; unused credits expire 12 months from purchase. Redwood will reconcile credits monthly and refund remaining balance only at contract termination or by written agreement."

If Legal is OK, we can add both items to the order form redline and return to Pivotal.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

From: Samira Khan <contracts@pivotalhealth.com>
